Based on the provided documents, the Soil Health Card Scheme is a government initiative designed to provide farmers with detailed information about their soil to help them improve crop yield and soil health.

Here are the key details about the scheme:

*   **Purpose:** The scheme aims to cover all farmers across the country. It provides farmers with a report (the "soil card") containing details about the soil on their specific farm.
*   **Benefits for Farmers:**
    *   It helps farmers decide which crops to cultivate and which to avoid based on their soil's nutrient status.
    *   It provides recommendations on which fertilizers to use, encouraging balanced application instead of just urea.
    *   It gives farmers a proper soil health record and updated data, allowing them to plan for the future of their crops and land.
    *   The government employs experts to help farmers carry out corrective measures to improve soil quality.
*   **Process:**
    *   Soil is tested on a regular basis, and a farm receives a new soil card once every three years.
    *   The scheme ensures that the same person conducts the soil analysis for a particular farmer to maintain consistency and effectiveness.
*   **Key Parameters Tested:** The soil card reports on key parameters including pH, organic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and micronutrients.
*   **Scale:** The scheme has been implemented on a large scale, with over 107 million Soil Health Cards issued in the first cycle (2015-17) and over 119 million in the second cycle (2017-19).

They are near the middle of your back, just below the rib cage. Inside each kidney there are about a million tiny structures called nephrons. They filter your blood. They remove wastes and extra water, which become urine. The urine flows through tubes called ureters. It goes to your bladder, which stores the urine until you go to the bathroom. Most kidney diseases attack the nephrons. This damage may leave kidneys unable to remove wastes. Causes can include genetic problems, injuries, or medicines. You have a higher risk of kidney disease if you have diabetes , high blood pressure , or a close family member with kidney disease. Chronic kidney disease damages the nephrons slowly over several years. Other kidney problems include: Cancer Cysts Stones Infections Your doctor can do blood and urine tests to check if you have kidney disease. If your kidneys fail , you will need dialysis or a kidney transplant . retrieved_contexts: ["Heart Diseases Also called: Cardiac diseases On this page Basics Summary Start Here Diagnosis and Tests Prevention and Risk Factors Treatments and Therapies Learn More Living With Related Issues Specifics Genetics See, Play and Learn Videos and Tutorials Test Your Knowledge Research Statistics and Research Clinical Trials Journal Articles Resources Reference Desk Find an Expert For You Children Men Women Older Adults Patient Handouts Summary What is heart disease? Heart disease is a general term that includes many types of heart problems. It's a type of cardiovascular disease, which means heart and blood vessel disease. Heart disease is the leading cause of death in the United States, but there are ways to prevent and manage many types of heart disease. What are the types of heart disease? There are many different types of heart disease. Some you may be born with, called congenital heart disease . Other types develop during your lifetime. Coronary artery disease (also called coronary heart disease) is the most common type of heart disease. **सामान्य ज्ञान के आधार पर:**

उच्च रक्तचाप (हाइपरटेंशन) से पीड़ित किसी भी व्यक्ति के लिए यह चिंता का विषय है, चाहे वह किसी भी देश का हो या उसमें कोई लक्षण दिखाई दे रहे हों या नहीं। उच्च रक्तचाप को अक्सर "साइलेंट किलर" (मूक हत्यारा) कहा जाता है क्योंकि इसके आमतौर पर कोई स्पष्ट लक्षण नहीं होते हैं। इसका अर्थ यह है कि व्यक्ति वर्षों तक इससे पीड़ित रह सकता है और उसे इस बात का पता भी नहीं चलता, जबकि यह स्थिति उसके शरीर को निरंतर क्षति पहुँचा रही होती है।

लक्षणों के बिना भी यह चिंताजनक क्यों है, इसके कारण निम्नलिखित हैं:

*   **मूक क्षति (साइलेंट डैमेज):** उच्च रक्तचाप धमनियों की दीवारों पर निरंतर अत्यधिक दबाव डालता है। यह दबाव समय के साथ रक्त वाहिकाओं और अंगों को क्षति पहुँचाता है, जिससे अक्सर तब तक कोई लक्षण दिखाई नहीं देते जब तक कि गंभीर क्षति न हो जाए।
*   **प्रमुख स्वास्थ्य घटनाओं का बढ़ा हुआ जोखिम:** यह मूक क्षति जीवन के लिए घातक या अक्षम करने वाली स्वास्थ्य समस्याओं के जोखिम को काफी बढ़ा देती है, जिनमें शामिल हैं:
    *   **हृदय घात (हार्ट अटैक):** हृदय की मांसपेशियों तक रक्त पहुँचाने वाली धमनियों के संकुचित होने (एथेरोस्क्लेरोसिस) के कारण।
    *   **मस्तिष्क घात (स्ट्रोक):** मस्तिष्क में रक्त वाहिकाओं के कमजोर होने या फटने के कारण।
    *   **वृक्क विफलता (किडनी फेल्योर):** वृक्क (किडनी) में रक्त वाहिकाओं के क्षतिग्रस्त होने के कारण।
    *   **दृष्टि हानि:** आँखों की रक्त वाहिकाओं के क्षतिग्रस्त होने के कारण।
    *   **संज्ञानात्मक गिरावट (कॉग्निटिव डिक्लाइन):** मस्तिष्क में रक्त के प्रवाह में कमी आने के कारण।

मुख्य चिंता यह है कि जब तक कोई व्यक्ति लक्षणों को महसूस करता है (जैसे कि हृदय घात या मस्तिष्क घात के दौरान), तब तक क्षति पहले ही गंभीर और संभावित रूप से अपरिवर्तनीय हो चुकी होती है। इसलिए, उच्च रक्तचाप का प्रबंधन करना और नियमित रूप से इसकी जाँच करवाना अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण है ताकि इन गंभीर जटिलताओं को रोका जा सके।

प्रदत्त दस्तावेजों के आधार पर, "मृदा संशोधन" (soil amendments) शब्द का स्पष्ट रूप से उपयोग नहीं किया गया है। हालाँकि, मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड (SHC) की सिफारिशों के उद्देश्य और कार्य का वर्णन किया गया है।

दस्तावेजों के अनुसार, मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड किसानों को उनके मृदा के पोषक तत्वों की स्थिति के बारे में जानकारी प्रदान करता है और **"मृदा स्वास्थ्य और उर्वरता में सुधार के लिए लागू किए जाने वाले पोषक तत्वों की उचित मात्रा पर सिफारिशें"** देता है।

इन सिफारिशों की भूमिका किसानों को निम्नलिखित में सहायता करना है:
*   **पोषक तत्वों की कमी को दूर करना:** कार्ड किसानों को यह बताता है कि उनकी मृदा में किन पोषक तत्वों की कमी है।
*   **उर्वरकों का सही उपयोग करना:** यह सलाह देता है कि किन उर्वरकों की आवश्यकता है और कितनी मात्रा में, जिससे किसानों को केवल यूरिया जैसे एकल उर्वरक पर निर्भर रहने के बजाय संतुलित उर्वरकों का उपयोग करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित किया जा सके।
*   **मृदा स्वास्थ्य और उपज में सुधार करना:** इन सिफारिशों का अंतिम लक्ष्य मृदा के स्वास्थ्य और उर्वरता को बढ़ाना है, जिससे कृषि उत्पादकता में सुधार होता है।
reference: कार्ड में अनुशंसित मृदा संवर्धन को किसानों द्वारा उर्वरक प्रयोग के साथ-साथ उनके खेतों से इष्टतम उपज प्राप्त करने के लिए किया जाता है।

1.  **See a Doctor Immediately:** This is the most important step. A healthcare professional can confirm the diagnosis with a blood test and monitor for signs of severe dengue.
2.  **Rest and Stay Hydrated:** Get plenty of rest and drink lots of fluids like water, oral rehydration solutions, or clear broths to prevent dehydration from fever and vomiting.

    *   Persistent vomiting
    *   Rapid breathing
    *   Bleeding gums or nose
    *   Fatigue or restlessness
    *   Blood in vomit or stool

If you have asthma, you will work with your health care provider to create a treatment plan. The plan will include ways to manage your asthma symptoms and prevent asthma attacks. It will include: Strategies to avoid triggers. For example, if tobacco smoke is a trigger for you, you should not smoke or allow other people to smoke in your home or car. Short-term relief medicines, also called quick-relief medicines. They help prevent symptoms or relieve symptoms during an asthma attack. They include an inhaler to carry with you all the time. It may also include other types of medicines which work quickly to help open your airways. Control medicines. You take them every day to help prevent symptoms. They work by reducing airway inflammation and preventing narrowing of the airways. If you have a severe attack and the short-term relief medicines do not work, you will need emergency care. Your provider may adjust your treatment until asthma symptoms are controlled. Sometimes asthma is severe and cannot be controlled with other treatments. If you are an adult with uncontrolled asthma, in some cases your provider might suggest bronchial thermoplasty. This is a procedure that uses heat to shrink the smooth muscle in the lungs. What are the symptoms of arthritis? Pain, redness, warmth, and joint inflammation are common arthritis symptoms. You may not be able to move your joint as well as it should. Other symptoms could include fever , weight loss, breathing difficulties, or a rash. Symptoms often get worse as you age. Some symptoms of arthritis may be signs of other illnesses. *   **डायलिसिस:** यह एक ऐसी प्रक्रिया है जो रक्त से अपशिष्ट और अतिरिक्त तरल पदार्थों को छानने के लिए मशीन का उपयोग करती है। इसके दो मुख्य प्रकार हैं:

Lifestyle changes include reducing salt, exercising regularly, and limiting alcohol.', 'High Blood Pressure Also called: Benign essential hypertension, Essential hypertension, HBP, HTN, Hypertension On this page Basics Summary Start Here Symptoms Diagnosis and Tests Prevention and Risk Factors Treatments and Therapies Learn More Living With Related Issues Specifics Genetics See, Play and Learn Videos and Tutorials Test Your Knowledge Research Statistics and Research Clinical Trials Journal Articles Resources Find an Expert For You Children Teenagers Women Older Adults Patient Handouts Summary What is blood pressure? Blood pressure is the force of your blood pushing against the walls of your arteries. Each time your heart beats, it pumps blood into the arteries. Your blood pressure is highest when your heart beats, pumping the blood. This is called systolic pressure. When your heart is at rest, between beats, your blood pressure falls. This is called diastolic pressure. Your blood pressure reading uses these two numbers. Usually the systolic number comes before or above the diastolic number. For example, 120/80 means a systolic of 120 and a diastolic of 80. How is high blood pressure diagnosed? High blood pressure usually has no symptoms. ### Economic Advantages

*   **Informed Crop Selection:** The soil card provides details on the soil's nutrient status, allowing farmers to decide which crops are best suited for their land. This helps them maximize profits by cultivating crops that will thrive, rather than risking failure with unsuitable ones.
*   **Optimized Fertilizer Use:** The card gives specific recommendations on which fertilizers and in what quantities farmers should apply. This prevents them from wasting money on unnecessary or incorrect fertilizers, ensuring they invest in the right inputs for better yields.

*   **Improved Soil Health:** The scheme's core function is to test the soil and provide recommendations for corrective measures and soil amendments. This helps farmers actively improve the quality and fertility of their soil over time.

प्रदत्त संदर्भ के आधार पर, मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड (सॉयल हेल्थ कार्ड) किसानों को उनके मृदा के पोषक तत्वों की स्थिति के बारे में विशिष्ट जानकारी प्रदान करके रासायनिक उर्वरकों के उपयोग को कम करने में सहायता करते हैं।

यह प्रक्रिया निम्नलिखित रूप में कार्य करती है:

1. **लक्षित अनुप्रयोग (टारगेटेड एप्लीकेशन):** मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड किसानों को उनके मृदा में पोषक तत्वों की कमी के बारे में सूचित करता है। इससे उन्हें केवल यूरिया जैसे उर्वरकों के सामान्य प्रयोग के स्थान पर, मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड में दी गई सिफारिशों के आधार पर संतुलित उर्वरकों और सूक्ष्म पोषक तत्वों का उपयोग करने की सुविधा मिलती है।
2. **अति-उर्वरक प्रयोग में कमी:** मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड से पूर्व, 90% से अधिक किसानों ने अपने मृदा का परीक्षण नहीं कराया था और 92% किसानों ने संतुलित उर्वरकों का उपयोग नहीं किया था, क्योंकि उनके पास अपने मृदा में पोषक तत्वों की उपलब्धता के संबंध में जानकारी का अभाव था। मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड की सिफारिशों का पालन करके, किसान केवल उन्हीं पोषक तत्वों का प्रयोग कर सकते हैं जिनकी उनकी मृदा को आवश्यकता है, जिससे रासायनिक उर्वरकों के समग्र उपयोग में कमी आती है।

राष्ट्रीय उत्पादकता परिषद (नेशनल प्रोडक्टिविटी काउंसिल) द्वारा किए गए एक अध्ययन में यह पाया गया कि मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड की सिफारिशों के अनुसार उर्वरकों के प्रयोग के परिणामस्वरूप रासायनिक उर्वरकों के उपयोग में 8-10% की कमी आई है।

Cancer is not just one disease but many diseases. Cancer begins in your cells, which are the building blocks of your body. Usually, your body forms new cells as needed, replacing old cells that die. Sometimes this process goes wrong. New cells grow even when you don't need them, and old cells don't die when they should. These extra cells can form a mass called a tumor. Tumors can be benign or malignant. Benign tumors aren't cancer, while malignant ones are. Cells from malignant tumors can invade nearby tissues. They can also break away and spread to other parts of your body. The spread of cancer from one part of the body to another is called metastasis. Symptoms and treatment depend on the type of cancer and how advanced it is. What are the types of cancer? There are more than 100 different types of cancer. Cancer can start almost anywhere in your body. Most cancers are named for where they start. For example, lung cancer starts in the lung, and breast cancer starts in the breast. Cancer may also be described by the type", "cancers are named for where they start. For example, lung cancer starts in the lung, and breast cancer starts in the breast. Cancer may also be described by the type of cell that formed it, such as sarcoma if cancer begins in your bone and soft tissue. Carcinoma is the most common type of cancer. *   **Buildup of Toxins:** Harmful waste products, like urea, build up in the bloodstream, a condition called uremia. This can poison the body and affect the brain, heart, and other organs.
*   **Fluid Retention:** The body cannot remove excess fluid, leading to swelling (edema) in the legs, hands, and feet, and potentially fluid in the lungs (pulmonary edema), which can cause severe shortness of breath.
*   **Kidney Failure:** Untreated kidney disease can progress to complete kidney failure (end-stage renal disease). At this point, the kidneys have lost almost all function.
*   **Need for Dialysis or Transplant:** To survive with kidney failure, a person requires regular dialysis (a treatment that artificially filters the blood) or a kidney transplant.
*   **Increased Risk of Heart Disease and Stroke:** Kidney disease is a major risk factor for cardiovascular problems. The strain on the body from kidney dysfunction significantly increases the risk of heart attack and stroke.

**What is cancer and how does it start in the body?**

Cancer is a disease that begins when cells in the body start to grow out of control.

Normally, the body's cells grow, divide, and die in an orderly way. This process is controlled by the cell's DNA, which contains the instructions for everything the cell does. Cancer starts when changes (mutations) occur in the DNA of a cell. These mutations can be inherited or caused by external factors like exposure to chemicals, radiation, or certain viruses.

These genetic changes disrupt the normal, orderly process of cell growth and death. The mutations cause cells to:
*   **Grow and divide uncontrollably**, even when new cells are not needed.
*   **Live longer than they should**, instead of dying at their normal time.

As these abnormal cells accumulate, they can form a mass of tissue, called a tumor. Not all tumors are cancerous; benign tumors do not spread to other parts of the body. Malignant tumors, which are cancerous, can invade nearby tissues and spread to other parts of the body, a process called metastasis.
